To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed and implemented a new threshold ECDSA scheme that is the first to be practical in the WAN setting, the first to be efficient enough for use with embedded devices, and the first to be secure under the weakest known ECDSA assumption.

(1) the threshold-2 protocol of Doerner et~al. can be extended to arbitrary threshold t, (2) the resulting protocol is secure under a weaker assumption than prior works, (3) it requires only log(t)+6 communication rounds, and (4) it is the fastest known threshold ECDSA protocol for any threshold t.
we have developed a new protocol for threshold ECDSA that is faster than all prior works, is secure against malicious adversaries, and can be used in practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the minimum number of assumptions required to securely compute a threshold ECDSA signature?

the following three problems: (1) the problem of extending a known ECDSA threshold signature protocol to a larger threshold; (2) the problem of designing a new consistency check for an arbitrary number t of participants; (3) the problem of optimizing the underlying two-party ECDSA multiplication protocol.
the following three contributions: a new security proof for threshold ECDSA; the first practical threshold ECDSA protocol for any t; the fastest threshold ECDSA protocol in the LAN setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our protocol outperformed all the others in every scenario.
our protocol outperformed all prior works by at least a factor of 2 in the LAN setting and at least a factor 4 in the WAN setting.
we present a new threshold ECDSA scheme that is the most practical one to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed the first practical threshold ECDSA scheme that is secure against a malicious t-out-of-n adversary, with a round complexity logarithmic in the number of parties.
we propose the first threshold-ECDSA scheme that can sign in a reasonable time with any threshold.
we propose a practical, provably secure threshold ECDSA scheme with a round complexity logarithmic in the number of parties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the first time, threshold ECDSA is a realistic option for use in practice.
the Doerner et al.\ technique, when properly adapted to an arbitrary threshold, yields a scheme that is both secure and practical.
, for the first time, it is practical to use a threshold ECDSA scheme in a real-world setting, and that this can be achieved under a very mild set of assumptions.
